name: Jindal Poly Investment and Finance Company Limited

news.title: New minor risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 75% of Indian stocks, typically moving 9.0% a week. This is considered a minor risk. Share price volatility indicates the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. It also increases the risk of potential losses in the short term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Minor Risks Share price has been volatile over the past 3 months (9.0% average weekly change). Profit margins are more than 30% lower than last year (89% net profit margin).

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹668 (vs ₹31.81 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹668 (up from ₹31.81 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹9.62b (up ₹9.54b from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹7.02b (up ₹6.69b from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 73% (down from 429% in 3Q 2025). Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 23% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 32% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

news.body: Jindal Poly Investment and Finance Company Limited announced that they will report Q3, 2026 results at 3:30 PM, Indian Standard Time on Feb 13, 2026

news.title: Investor sentiment improves as stock rises 16%
news.body: After last week's 16% share price gain to ₹1,125, the stock trades at a trailing P/E ratio of 5.4x. Average trailing P/E is 28x in the Capital Markets industry in India. Total returns to shareholders of 117% over the past three years.

news.title: Second quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹54.74 (vs ₹133 in 2Q 2025)
news.body: Second quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹54.74 (down from ₹133 in 2Q 2025). Net income: ₹575.4m (down 59% from 2Q 2025). Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 1% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 16% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.
